newsitem.title: PERU: Parents hope U.S. woman in Peru jail not forgotten.
newsitem.headline: Parents hope U.S. woman in Peru jail not forgotten.

text.p: The parents of an American woman jailed for life in Peru for involvement with Marxist rebels said on Saturday they hoped their daughter's call for a retrial is not forgotten because of the country's 18-day hostage crisis.

"We pray for a non-violent end to the crisis," Mark Berenson told Reuters from his New York home. "Nevertheless, we hope Lori's claim that she is innocent and her insistence on receiving a fair, civilian trial are not forgotten."

Lori Berenson, 27, was accused in December 1995 of belonging to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) -- the same group holding 74 captives at the Japanese ambassador's residence and demanding the release of all their jailed comrades.
Judges wearing hoods in a secret military court convicted Berenson of treason and sentenced her to life imprisonment for allegedly helping plot a takeover of Congress.

She has called the charges "preposterous" and there is a growing campaign abroad -- actively supported by former U.S. President Jimmy Carter -- to press Peru's President Alberto Fujimori to grant her a new trial.
Berenson's conviction and harsh conditions at Peru's Yanamayo maximum-security prison have prompted foreign criticism of Peru's treatment of guerrillas during trial and imprisonment.
